Thanks — happy to hop on a call if helpful.

Team —

Quick notes after initial scan of the csv Josh sent:
- Current committed pool: 48 A100-equivalent GPUs.
- Recent median sustained utilization across the fleet is ~62%; 95th percentile hourly utilization hit 88% twice in Oct (weekday spikes aligned to campaign cadence).
- Monthly token growth linearly projects to +30% by end of contract if trends continue.

Recommendation (first pass):
1) Commit to 12 additional GPUs (bringing committed to 60) to cover steady growth and reduce steady-state saturation.
2) Add a 10-GPU burst buffer (pay-as-used) that auto-trigger for scheduled campaign windows. This avoids long-term cost while covering short peaks.
3) Put an autoscale guardrail: if sustained 7-day avg utilization >75% for 7 days, trigger a mid-term top-up clause to convert up to 8 burst GPUs to committed.

Pricing options:
- Upfront 12 GPU add: 12-month prorated discount available if signed by 11/15.
- Burst credits: billed at on-demand rate, can be capped per month to control spend.

I can draft the one-pager and attach proposed_capacity_plan_Nebula_v3.xlsx with the numbers and a simple timeline.

-Vanessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

(Attachment referenced: proposed_capacity_plan_Nebula_v3.xlsx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 10:11:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Upcoming renewal + request for capacity plan

Adding technical details to Vanessa’s commercial rec:

- Model mix: 70% standard generation models (seq len avg ~512), 30% embedding/rerank calls. This favors fewer memory-heavy configs and benefits from continuous KV caching.
- Kernel plan: recommend quantized 4-bit variants for a subset of models (non-LL) for cost roadmapping; expected token cost reduction ~18% with negligible perf loss in our benchmarks.
- Batching: current request distribution supports larger batching windows during off-peak; enable burst batching policies to lower cost when burst buffer is active.
- Observability: add a per-route token SLO with alerting (p50/p95 latency and token burn rate) to trigger the autoscale guardrail rather than raw GPU utilization alone.

Operational playbook (proposed):
1) Week 0 (sign): add 12 GPUs to committed pool, enable burst buffer with 10 GPUs and set monthly cap.
2) Weeks 1–2: enable quantized model variants on non-critical routes, enable KV prefix caching for high-freq flows.
3) Weeks 3–6: monitor SLOs and 7-day avg; if guardrail trips, prepare change order to convert up to 8 burst GPUs to committed (with prorated bill).

I’ll include the technical annex in the spreadsheet.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

- Provision a 10-GPU burst buffer (pay-as-used) with a monthly cap to contain spend.
- Autoscale guardrail: convert up to 8 burst GPUs to committed if 7-day avg SLOs exceed thresholds for 7 consecutive days.

Commercial notes:
- If signed by 11/15 we can apply a midterm discount that reduces the incremental unit price by 8% for the 12 GPUs.
- If Nebula prefers an alternative cadence we can split the 12 GPU commit into two tranches (6 + 6) with a 60-day review.

Next steps:

2) Procurement: if you need a redline, loop your legal and procurement and we’ll coordinate.
